title: What to Do When Your Teen Has No Friends in Their Class
summary: A calm parent decision path for understanding a difficult class dynamic, trying one proportionate step, and knowing when school support is warranted.
seo_title: Teen Has No Friends in Class: What to Do
seo_description: A practical parent plan for when your teen has no friends in their class: listen, map the barrier, try one low-pressure step, and know when to involve school.
release_move: Listen for the pattern, help your teen choose one proportionate next move, and involve the school with observable facts when access, safety, or functioning is affected.

core_belief_shift.from: If my teen has no friends in a class, I need to demand a class change or solve the friendship problem myself.
core_belief_shift.to: I can listen for the pattern, map the barrier, support one low-pressure move, and escalate observable access or safety concerns.

book_relevance.reason: The useful next move is a calm parent-school decision path that protects the teenager's ownership; a product bridge would distract from that work.

next_step.label: Read Quiet or Lonely?
next_step.reason: Use this next when you need to tell the difference between restorative time alone and unwanted disconnection without treating quietness as the problem.
